questions.text: A given connected graph G is a Euler Graph if and only if all vertices of G are of
questions.solution:
Euler's theorem: a connected graph has an Euler circuit if and only if every vertex has even degree (each visit enters and leaves a vertex).

Answer: even degree

questions.text: [latex]f (G,.)[/latex] is a group such that [latex](ab)^{-1}=a^{-1}b^{-1},\forall a,b \in G[/latex], then [latex]G[/latex] is a/an
questions.solution:
In any group [latex](ab)^{-1}=b^{-1}a^{-1}[/latex]. If also [latex](ab)^{-1}=a^{-1}b^{-1}[/latex] for all a, b, then [latex]b^{-1}a^{-1}=a^{-1}b^{-1}[/latex] for all elements, i.e. every pair commutes.

Answer: Abelian group

questions.text:
Consider a set U of 23 different compounds in a Chemistry lab. There is a subset S of U of 9 compounds, each of which reacts with exactly 3 compounds of U. Consider the following statements:

I. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
II. At least one compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
III. Each compound in U n S reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?
questions.solution:
Model compounds as vertices and reactions as edges. The sum of all degrees is even (handshake lemma).

The 9 compounds in S have degree 3 each: total 27 (odd). So the degrees of U \ S must add to an odd number, which needs at least one odd degree there. Nothing forces every one to be odd.

Answer: Only II

questions.text:
A binary relation R on [latex]\mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{N}[/latex] is defined as follows: (a,b)R(c,d) if [latex]a \leq c[/latex] or [latex]b \leq d[/latex]. Consider the following propositions:
P: R is reflexive
Q: R is transitive
Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Reflexive: (a, b) R (a, b) since [latex]a\le a[/latex] True
- Transitive fails: (3, 2) R (1, 3) because 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 3, and (1, 3) R (2, 1) because 1 [latex]\le[/latex] 2, but (3, 2) R (2, 1) needs 3 [latex]\le[/latex] 2 or 2 [latex]\le[/latex] 1 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] both false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false.
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false

questions.text: Breadth First Search(BFS) is started on a binary tree beginning from the root vertex. There is a vertex t at a distance four from the root. If t is the n-th vertex in this BFS traversal, then the maximum possible value of n is______ .
questions.solution:
BFS visits level by level. To make t as late as possible, levels 0-3 are full (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 nodes) and t is the last of the 16 nodes at level 4.

n = 15 + 16 = 31

Answer: 31
